title: Incubator

references.label: General microbiology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)
Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

purpose: Maintains a controlled, stable temperature (and sometimes humidity/CO2/atmosphere) to support microbial growth under conditions appropriate to the target organism.
operatingPrinciple: A heating element and thermostat maintain a set-point temperature inside an insulated chamber; some incubators add CO2 or humidity control for specialized cultivation needs (a Tier 2 topic).
basicOperation: Set the target temperature appropriate to the organism being cultured.
Allow the chamber to stabilize at the set temperature before loading cultures.
Avoid frequent door-opening, which disrupts internal temperature stability.
importantSettings: Target temperature — organism-dependent, not universal (e.g. many clinically relevant bacteria are cultured near human body temperature, while many environmental organisms prefer lower temperatures).
calibration: Periodic verification with an independent calibrated thermometer/data logger against the displayed set-point, per facility SOP.
maintenance: Regularly clean interior surfaces to reduce contamination risk.
Check door seals for a stable, insulated closure.

commonErrors.problem: Cultures grow inconsistently or too slowly/quickly
commonErrors.cause: Actual chamber temperature drifted from the set-point, or frequent door-opening
commonErrors.fix: Verify actual temperature with an independent thermometer and minimize door-opening during incubation

safety: Follow biosafety procedures for the organism being incubated when loading/unloading.
